reasoning_content:
Great. 10 target records need to be generated, with score and clinical truth required to be independently identifiable. Existing data includes a responder/nonresponder mapped from the clinical response column, assay scores, IC50 values in some figures, and binary assay prediction requirements. Some rows are grayed out, and the clinical truth of all samples has been clarified. There is a contradiction between the assay prediction results and the administered drug testing record as two samples received drugs not included in the tested items. Source of score values needs to be confirmed, and raw viability can be used as a candidate source but the relevant threshold is not explicitly reported.

Using heatmap-derived categorical assay sensitivity values is a viable option, as the legend allows mapping of color identifiers to binary scores. However, some color-code matching rules and specific numerical data still need further verification.

The mapping of red and olive colors to non-sensitive status is not ideal, and raw viability has defects like logical contradictions and uncertain calibration rules. We need Ctrough viability data, and there are issues with data source and compliance for 100% accuracy requirements.

I’ve confirmed using score values from figures/tables and clinical responses as the source for categorical assay sensitivity and clinical truth, and verified the alignment between target figure rows and heatmap rows/columns, plus drug color coding rules.

I’ve finalized the color coding rule for assay sensitivity: shades of blue represent sensitive status, while red and olive mark non-sensitive status. I will use vision-derived values for mapping, and can also adopt IC50 values from relevant figures for mapping if needed.

I’ve finalized the coding rule for clinical truth mapping, assigning 1 to PR/non-PD/CR and 0 to PD. The comparison unit is 10 patients, the assay readout is log IC50 from heatmaps, and no explicit threshold rule is currently needed.

The regimen matching rule has been finalized, selecting "partial" as the matching result for the 10-patient observational cohort. I will use vision-derived values for scoring reference, and verify relevant score sources to ensure accuracy.

I’ve verified the color coding of all target samples, confirmed the relevant supporting data file is the same as the reference one, and will use its corresponding sheets and rows for follow-up truth value retrieval.

I’ve finished mapping sample clinical truth values and color-coded binary assay sensitivity values, with binary scoring and accuracy calculation confirmed. I will refer to pages 27 and 28 of the target article to complete follow-up analysis.
